To reduce input costs, avoid loading entire documents into the context window. Instead of loading a 50-page PDF into the prompt for a simple query, use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Context engineering involves: selecting the right information at the right moment (where RAG and file reads matter), compressing what's already in the window by summarizing resolved turns and trimming tool output, and isolating work across separate context windows so one task doesn't contaminate another's context.

## Token Cost Control Approaches

Prompt caching offers a 90% discount on cached input tokens and is the single largest cost lever for repeated system prompts. Claude API context compaction can condense conversation history server-side—in one reported case, 132,000 tokens collapsed to 2,000.

A one-million-token context window is available for monorepo loading, though retrieval quality matters more than raw context length on most real workloads. Vector databases work well but get expensive—you pay for storage, indexing compute, and often the queries themselves. For many workflows, a hybrid approach using efficient file storage costs less.

Lovable generates a single-page React app scaffolded with **Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + React Router**, deliberately *not* Next.js App Router ([vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/), [blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). shadcn/ui matters because it's copy-in component source (not a locked dependency), so the AI can freely edit it and output stays consistent and good-looking. Kodely should ship this as the default template for pure web-app builds — it's fast to preview, easy for the model to reason about, and produces attractive UI out of the box.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Offer a Next.js full-stack template (rocket.new / v0 style)","description":"For apps that need server routes, SSR, and a real backend in one repo, rocket.new generates **production Next.js** apps and v0 generates full-stack Next.js with API routes and DB integration ([docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction), [blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). This is exactly Nxeon's existing stack (Next.js + Prisma + Postgres), so Kodely can reuse Nxeon's build/deploy tooling and conventions with almost no new work for this template. Recommend two first-class templates — Vite SPA (fast/simple) and Next.js full-stack (Nxeon-native) — and let the planner pick based on the prompt.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Backend choice: Supabase vs Convex vs Neon vs reuse Nxeon Postgres","description":"rocket.new and Lovable both lean on **Supabase** (managed Postgres + auth + storage + realtime in one) as the default generated backend ([docs.rocket.new](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction)). Alternatives: **Convex** (TypeScript reactive backend, native embeddings/semantic search, great for realtime), **Neon** (serverless Postgres with branching + scale-to-zero, but no bundled auth/storage) ([bytebase.com/blog/convex-vs-supabase](https://www.bytebase.com/blog/convex-vs-supabase/), [encore.dev/articles/supabase-alternatives](https://encore.dev/articles/supabase-alternatives)). Kodely's edge: it can offer **Nxeon-hosted Postgres+Prisma as the default backend** (own infra, no Supabase bill, first-month-free hosting angle) while still supporting Supabase for users who want portability. Neon-style DB branching per preview is worth copying.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Auth: bundle a batteries-included auth provider per template","description":"Generated apps need working auth on the first build — rocket.new ships auth as part of every backend setup and lists multiple auth providers among its 25+ native integrations ([netnewsledger.com/2026/05/03](https://www.netnewsledger.com/2026/05/03/rocket-new-is-the-best-ai-app-builder-with-built-in-integrations/)). For the Supabase template use Supabase Auth; for the Nxeon Next.js template wire Auth.js/Lucia against the existing Postgres. Kodely should generate auth pre-connected (login/signup/session + a protected route example) rather than leaving it to the model to invent each time, which is where AI builders most often produce broken or insecure code. Ship a tested auth scaffold per template.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"File / object storage for generated apps","description":"rocket.new treats file storage as first-class via Supabase storage ([republicworld.com](https://www.republicworld.com/initiatives/rocketnew-is-the-best-full-stack-ai-app-builder-in-2026)). Kodely should provide an S3-compatible object store (MinIO on Nxeon infra, or Supabase Storage for that template) with a generated upload helper and signed-URL pattern baked into templates. Keep tenant buckets/prefixes isolated so one generated app can never read another's files. Reuse whatever object storage Nxeon already runs for hosting backups if present.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Live preview + hot reload wiring","description":"The preview must reflect edits within a second. bolt.new achieves this by giving the model full control of the WebContainer filesystem + dev server so Vite HMR just works; Lovable achieves it by pointing the editor iframe at a real running instance ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new), [vibe-eval.com](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/)). For a server-sandbox model, Kodely should run the framework dev server (Vite/Next) inside the sandbox, expose it via a per-project proxy subdomain (e.g. `<id>.preview.kodely...`), and stream file writes straight to disk so the dev server's own HMR pushes updates to the iframe over WebSocket. Recommend proxy-per-project with wildcard TLS.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"One-click deploy: own Nxeon infra first, then Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare","description":"Bolt deploys one-click to Netlify/Cloudflare, Lovable to Netlify/Vercel, v0 to Vercel ([gautamkhorana.com/blog/hosting-for-lovable-v0-jamstack-apps-2026](https://gautamkhorana.com/blog/hosting-for-lovable-v0-jamstack-apps-2026/), [netlify.com/knowledge-base/deploy-your-v0-app-to-netlify](https://www.netlify.com/knowledge-base/deploy-your-v0-app-to-netlify/)). Kodely's differentiator is that Nxeon is *itself a hosting company* — the default 'Deploy' button should ship straight to Nxeon hosting (leveraging first-month-free hosting), turning every build into a hosting customer. Also offer export/deploy to Vercel/Netlify/Cloudflare for portability so users never feel locked in. This is Kodely's clearest strategic advantage over the incumbents.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Bi-directional GitHub sync","description":"v0 offers bi-directional GitHub sync and Lovable does automatic branch management, preview deployments, and PR workflows, auto-committing changes ([blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). Kodely should let users connect a repo, push generated code, and — importantly — *pull external commits back* so the AI works on the real current state. Implement it as a GitHub App (fine-grained per-repo tokens, not a broad OAuth token) and commit each AI change as a reviewable, message-tagged commit. Two-way sync is table stakes for retaining serious developers.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Custom domains + automated SSL","description":"Meku and other builders advertise one-click custom domains with SSL as a headline feature ([zite.com/blog/free-ai-app-builder](https://www.zite.com/blog/free-ai-app-builder)). Nxeon already provisions domains, DNS, and TLS for hosting customers, so Kodely can reuse that pipeline directly — attach a custom domain to a deployed build and issue Let's Encrypt certs through existing Nxeon automation. Watch the mail-hostname / DNS lessons from memory (don't blanket-redirect, don't clobber real records). This is near-free to build given existing Nxeon capabilities.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Project persistence — snapshot the filesystem, not just the chat","description":"Users must be able to close the tab and return to a working project. WebContainer/sandbox filesystems are ephemeral, so state has to be persisted externally. Kodely should persist each project as a **git repo + a periodic filesystem snapshot** (tarball to object storage) plus the DB schema/migrations, so a project can be re-hydrated into a fresh sandbox on demand. Store the AI conversation/plan history alongside so context survives reloads. Recommend git-as-source-of-truth with snapshot for fast restore; hibernate idle sandboxes to cut cost.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Multi-tenant isolation for sandboxes and previews","description":"Every generated app runs untrusted, AI-written, user-editable code, so isolation is a security requirement, not a nicety — the whole reason E2B/Daytona/Modal exist is that you must never run agent-generated code directly on shared servers ([amux.io/guides/ai-agent-sandboxing](https://amux.io/guides/ai-agent-sandboxing/)). Kodely must isolate each tenant's sandbox at the kernel/VM level (Firecracker or per-tenant VM), with network egress controls, resource quotas, and no shared filesystem or DB credentials across tenants. Given Nxeon's history (the CRITICAL DB Studio RCE in memory), treat this as a hard gate before onboarding real users. Do a security review before any preview goes public.","type":"CHORE","priority":"URGENT"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Secrets handling — encrypted vault + inject at runtime, never in prompts","description":"Generated apps need API keys (Stripe, OpenAI, DB URLs) and rocket.new wires 25+ integrations that all require credentials ([netnewsledger.com/2026/05/03](https://www.netnewsledger.com/2026/05/03/rocket-new-is-the-best-ai-app-builder-with-built-in-integrations/)). Secrets must live in a per-project encrypted vault, be injected into the sandbox as env vars at runtime, and **must never be pasted into the LLM context** (where they'd leak into logs/outputs). Add an output guardrail that scans generated code/commits for real secrets before they're committed or shown. Recommend a vault service keyed per project with audit logging.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Per-branch preview environments with DB branching","description":"Lovable/v0 already do preview deployments per branch; Neon adds cheap Postgres *branching* so each preview gets an isolated copy of the schema/data ([encore.dev/articles/supabase-alternatives](https://encore.dev/articles/supabase-alternatives)). Kodely could give each AI iteration or user branch its own throwaway preview URL + branched database, so experiments never corrupt the main app's data. This makes 'try this change' safe and reversible — a strong trust feature for non-technical builders. Lower priority than core preview but a notable polish/differentiator.","type":"IDEA","priority":"LOW"},
{"column":"Tech & Architecture","title":"Sandbox cost control — hibernate, scale-to-zero, quotas","description":"Cloud sandboxes bill for the entire time they're alive (~$0.05/vCPU-hr on E2B/Daytona), so idle previews silently burn money ([particula.tech/blog/modal-vs-e2b-vs-daytona-vs-vercel-sandbox-ai-code-execution](https://particula.tech/blog/modal-vs-e2b-vs-daytona-vs-vercel-sandbox-ai-code-execution/)). Whether on rented sandboxes or Nxeon VMs, Kodely needs auto-hibernation of inactive projects, scale-to-zero, and per-plan CPU/RAM/runtime quotas, with fast re-hydration from the persisted snapshot. Bolt's flat-rate '$9 unlimited' model blew up on exactly this kind of runaway usage ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Build metering in from day one.","type":"CHORE","priority":"NORMAL"},

{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Build a flow-engineered agent loop: plan → generate → run → read errors → fix","description":"Bolt.new's core insight is **flow engineering** (à la AlphaCodium): break app generation into smaller sequential steps rather than one monolithic generation, which works better across model capabilities ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). The loop is: produce a plan, write files, run the dev server/build, capture errors, feed them back, and iterate with fix/ignore options. Kodely should implement this explicit state-machine loop rather than a single prompt→dump — it's the difference between apps that boot and apps that don't. This is the single most important engine decision.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"URGENT"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Diff-based edits over full-file rewrites","description":"Bolt applies changes as **diffs using speculative decoding**, changing only the parts that need updating — far fewer tokens and faster iterations than rewriting whole files, which matters at scale ([buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt](https://www.buildthisnow.com/blog/tools/extensions/claude-code-vs-bolt), [latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Lovable by contrast plans first and rewrites larger sections, and is measurably slower (~60s vs ~30s per generation). Kodely should default to targeted diff/patch edits (search-replace blocks or unified diffs the model emits) and reserve full-file writes for new files or large refactors. Directly cuts token cost and latency.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Model choice: Claude Sonnet as default, escalate to Opus for planning","description":"Bolt.new and much of the category run on Anthropic's Claude (Bolt built an >$8M ARR business essentially as a 'Claude wrapper') because Claude leads at agentic coding ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt), [mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding](https://mastra.ai/articles/best-llm-for-coding)). Kodely already has Nxeon's Anthropic-based 'Build-with-AI' integration to reuse. Recommend **Claude Sonnet (4.5-class) as the workhorse** for edits/codegen and **Opus for the initial plan/architecture step**, with the model abstracted behind a router so a cheaper model can handle trivial edits. NOTE from memory: the Nxeon chat agent is still blocked on a valid/funded Anthropic key — Kodely inherits that dependency, so resolve billing first.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Instrument the sandbox to feed real errors back to the agent","description":"Bolt instruments WebContainers at the **process, runtime, and build levels** so the agent receives 'the state of the application and the errors from Node.js or the browser console' and can auto-fix ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). This closed error loop is why its output actually runs. Kodely must capture build output, dev-server logs, uncaught runtime exceptions, and browser console errors from the sandbox and pipe them structured into the agent's next turn. Without this, the model is fixing blind. Build the error-capture channel as part of the sandbox from the start.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Context management for growing codebases — retrieve, don't dump","description":"Bolt maximizes context ('the entire state of the application') for accuracy, but that only scales while projects are small ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Chroma's Context Rot study found *every* frontier model degrades as input grows — a 200K window can show serious accuracy loss by 50K tokens, and facts buried mid-context cost 30+ accuracy points ([cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely needs a retrieval layer: send the full tree/manifest but only the *relevant* file bodies (via embeddings + recent-edit heuristics), and keep the most important context at the start/end of the prompt. Plan retrieval before projects get big.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Prompt caching — the single biggest cost lever","description":"Prompt caching gives a ~90% discount on cached input tokens and is the largest cost reducer for repeated system prompts; in Claude Code/Cline sessions, re-sending conversation history is ~50–60% of token spend and tool descriptions alone add 10–15K tokens per request ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should structure prompts so the stable system prompt, tool definitions, and unchanging project context sit in cacheable prefixes with Anthropic cache breakpoints. This is low-effort, high-savings and should be wired in before launch, not retrofitted.","type":"CHORE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Context compaction / conversation summarization","description":"Long build sessions bloat context; Claude's context-compaction can condense history server-side (one reported case collapsed 132K tokens to 2K) and 'isolating work across separate context windows' keeps tasks from contaminating each other ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely should summarize resolved turns, trim stale tool output, and maintain a compact rolling project-state summary rather than replaying the whole chat each turn. Keeps long iterative sessions affordable and accurate.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Tool-use design: give the agent fs, terminal, npm, and console tools","description":"Bolt gives the model complete control of the filesystem, node server, package manager, terminal and browser console ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should expose a tight, well-described tool set — write_file, apply_diff, read_file, run_command, install_package, read_logs, restart_dev_server — each mapped to sandbox operations. Keep tool descriptions lean (they're billed on every call) and prefer a few composable tools over many niche ones. Good tool ergonomics are what let the model self-correct instead of guessing.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Retrieval/index over the project (file tree + embeddings)","description":"When an agent lacks retrieval it wastes tokens reading whole files to find a few lines — the third-biggest token sink after history and tools ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/)). Vector DBs work but get expensive; a hybrid of efficient file storage + targeted embedding search often costs less ([pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should maintain a live project index (symbol map + embeddings, refreshed on edits) so the agent can grep/semantic-search to the exact files it needs. Reuse Nxeon's existing Postgres with pgvector rather than adding a new vector DB.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"System/prompt design + a structured artifact output format","description":"Bolt's quality comes largely from a carefully engineered system prompt that constrains the model into its step-by-step flow and a structured 'artifact' format for emitting files/commands (public in the open-source repo) ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should define a strict output schema — plan block, then file-write and shell-command actions the runner parses deterministically — so parsing never depends on fragile prose. Invest real effort in the system prompt (stack conventions, when to diff vs rewrite, security rules); it's the cheapest quality lever and it's cacheable.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Stream generation to the UI (files + reasoning live)","description":"Modern builders stream file writes and reasoning as they happen so users see progress instead of a spinner; this is core to the bolt/Lovable UX ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should stream the model's tokens, surface each file being created/edited in real time, and show the plan up front. Streaming also lets users interrupt/redirect early, saving tokens on wrong directions. Reuse the streaming plumbing from Nxeon's existing Build-with-AI/chat agent.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Token metering + credit system (don't repeat Bolt's flat-rate mistake)","description":"Bolt launched at $9/mo flat 'Netflix-model' access and users burned through allocations in weeks, creating scaling tension with inference cost ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Kodely must meter token/compute usage per user from day one, expose a credits balance, and price plans against real Anthropic + sandbox cost. Track cost per project/message so heavy users are identifiable. Tie this to Nxeon's existing billing. This is a business-survival item, not an optimization.","type":"CHORE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Execution-based evals: pass@k + a regression harness","description":"Real codegen quality is measured by *running* the output, not reading it — generate code, run it in a sandbox, check against tests, with pass@k as the headline metric; system-level evals also cover retrieval, prompt design, tool use and guardrails ([promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents/), [futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). Kodely should build an eval suite of representative prompts ('todo app with auth', 'Stripe checkout page') that generates, boots the app in a sandbox, and asserts it builds + core flows work — run on every prompt/model change to catch regressions before shipping to users. Prevents silent quality drops when tweaking prompts or swapping models.","type":"FEATURE","priority":"HIGH"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Guardrails: prompt-injection, secrets, and code-injection scanners","description":"Coding agents are attack surfaces — a Feb 2026 attack on the Cline IDE started with a malicious GitHub issue *title* containing injected instructions; defenses need input guardrails (screen prompts) and output guardrails (screen generated code) ([futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). A SecretsScanner catches invented/leaked credentials and a CodeInjectionScanner flags eval/exec/shell-interpolation/template-injection in generated code. Because Kodely will read user repos, GitHub issues, and pasted content into the agent, it must sanitize untrusted input and scan every generated file before commit/deploy. Given the CRITICAL RCE already found in Nxeon's DB Studio (memory), treat agent guardrails as a launch gate with a security review.","type":"CHORE","priority":"URGENT"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"shadcn/ui component retrieval for consistent, attractive UI","description":"A big reason Lovable/v0 output looks good is that they generate against **shadcn/ui**, whose components are editable source the model can retrieve and adapt rather than invent styling from scratch ([techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). Kodely should ship a curated component/block library (shadcn + a few opinionated layout blocks) and give the agent a retrieval tool to pull the right component source into edits, so UI stays consistent and polished across a project. This also cuts tokens (the model composes known components instead of hand-writing markup). Bonus: encode Nxeon's own brand theme (navy+violet+cyan per memory) as a preset for on-brand builds.","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Model routing + graceful degradation / fallback","description":"Kodely will depend on Anthropic availability, and memory notes the Nxeon chat agent already ships a failure banner + graceful-degrade pattern for exactly this. Kodely should route by task (cheap model for trivial edits, Sonnet for codegen, Opus for planning), fall back to a secondary model/provider on outages or rate limits, and surface a clear degraded-mode banner instead of failing silently. Retry with backoff on transient errors and cap retries to protect token spend. Reuse the Nxeon chat agent's degradation UX directly.","type":"IDEA","priority":"NORMAL"},
{"column":"AI / Codegen Engine","title":"Optional multi-agent decomposition (planner / coder / reviewer)","description":"Research on LLM multi-agent code generation shows splitting roles (a planner, a coder, and a reviewer/tester) can improve reliability on complex builds by isolating concerns into separate context windows ([arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely could add a lightweight reviewer pass that runs the eval/build and critiques the coder's output before showing the user. Keep it optional/behind a flag — it multiplies token cost, so gate it to complex prompts or paid tiers. Start single-agent, add this only if evals show it moves quality.","type":"IDEA","priority":"LOW"}
]
